catalog_migration.reason: Regenerate the approved Eastern Towhee plate to correct the page layout. The replacement refreshes the specimen, branch, ruler, typography, studies, palette, and overall composition so all content remains inside safe margins; all visible text and anatomy were independently re-reviewed.

profile.behavior: Primarily a ground forager, scratching through leaf litter with both feet; often concealed in dense undergrowth and may perch in low shrubs to sing.
field_marks: Large, chunky sparrow with a thick triangular bill
Long, rounded tail with conspicuous white outer corners
Adult male has a sooty-black head, throat, breast, and upperparts
Warm rufous sides contrast with a clean white belly
Folded wing shows small white bars or a white check-mark
Eyes are usually dark to reddish; legs are pinkish
profile.habitat: Dense brush, tangles, thickets, scrub, and forest edges with leaf litter for ground foraging.

sources.title: Eastern Towhee Identification — All About Birds

findings: The primary specimen is an anatomically coherent adult male Eastern Towhee with one head, one complete bill, one tail, two convincingly attached legs and intact grasping feet; the visible near-side wing is complete and the far-side wing is naturally occluded.
The detached wing and head are clearly supplementary studies. Both are anatomically coherent and remain visually separate from the primary specimen.

Plumage agrees with the reference photographs and direct-source descriptions: sooty-black head and upperparts, black throat and breast, warm rufous sides, white belly, white folded-wing markings, and white outer tail corners.

The chunky sparrow proportions, thick triangular bill, rounded body, long rounded tail, reddish eye, and pinkish legs are species-appropriate. Both depicted bills have coherent, consistent mandible proportions without truncation or reversal.
The common name, scientific name, and family are correctly written as Eastern Towhee, Pipilo erythrophthalmus, and Passerellidae.
Every printed measurement matches the proposed profile and Cornell's published values: length 6.8–8.2 in (17.3–20.8 cm), wingspan 7.9–11.0 in (20–28 cm), and weight 1.1–1.8 oz (32–52 g).

The body-length diagram is internally consistent: 6.8 in (17.3 cm) is the lower endpoint, 8.2 in (20.8 cm) is the upper endpoint, and values increase from bottom to top. It is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”

The habitat and behavior paragraphs are complete, correctly ordered, and consistent with direct-source accounts of brushy, leaf-litter habitat, two-footed ground scratching, concealment in undergrowth, and singing from shrubs or low trees.
All six field-mark bullets are legible, complete, and supported by the sources and reference photographs. No duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical words were found.
The five palette labels are correctly spelled and accurately represent the illustrated adult male's plumage, bill, and leg colors.
The plate has a clear scientific field-journal composition with strong hierarchy, balanced supplementary studies, and no misleading attachment of the detached studies to the primary specimen.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
